newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-REVOQUE GAINS COMPENSATION FOR CHAPPLE-HYAM.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-REVOQUE GAINS COMPENSATION FOR CHAPPLE-HYAM.

text.p: English trained Revoque proved
himself to be one of Europe's top two-year-olds after destroying
his rivals with an impressive burst of speed in the group one
Grand Criterium at Longchamp on Sunday.
Ridden by Irishman John Reid, the Peter-Chapple Hyam trained
colt was always travelling smoothly as Referendum, the mount of
Pat Eddery, and Majorien, with Freddie Head on board, made the
early running in the one mile (1.6 kms) race.
But once Reid pulled out Revoque to challenge the leaders
200 metres out the race was over in a matter of strides as he
pulled two lengths clear of Majorien, with the John Gosden
trained King Sound, ridden by Thierry Jarnet, six lengths
further back in third place in the nine runner field.
It was just reward for trainer Chapple-Hyam and Jockey Reid,
who at the same track last week suffered a double blow, first
when Monza was demoted to second place in the Prix de Conde and
later when Polaris Flight had to be destroyed after breaking a
leg in the Prix de L'Arc de Triomphe.
"It was all very easy," said Reid afterwards.
Revoque's odds for next year's English 2,000 Guineas were
cut from 10-1 to 7-1 by one leading British bookmaker.
Chapple-Hyam said: "This is a very good colt with a turn of
foot to match. He has done enough for the year and he must be
the best of his age group in Europe. He is an easy horse to
prepare and he could go straight for the 2,000 Guineas without a
preparatory race."
